text:
An old man was planting small trees in a field. A young man walked by and stopped.

“What are you doing?” he asked.

“I am planting apple trees,” said the old man.

“But these trees will take many years to grow,” said the young man. “You are old. You will not eat the fruit.”

The old man smiled. “That’s true. But when I was a boy, I ate apples from trees. Someone planted those trees before I was born. They did not know me, but they thought of me.”

The young man was surprised.

“Now I plant trees for children who are not born yet,” said the old man. “They will eat the apples and sit in the shade. They will be happy. That makes me happy too.”

The young man looked at the small trees. He thought for a long time. Then he took a shovel and began to help.

Moral: Do good things for others, even if you will not see the result.
